2Battery Materials Lab.
 A coupled DEM–MPM–transport workflow
• Each stage has specific calibration targets and unresolved validation tasks.
• Agreement between models sharing inputs is a consistency check, not 
independent validation.
Introduction
< DEM packing → plastic compaction → voxel transport → electrode response >

3Battery Materials Lab.
 Composition-dependent porosity in five simulated beds
• Soft-sphere DEM with a linear hysteretic contact law, pressed to 300 MPa; 
one bed per composition, no seed replicates.
• One 7:3 bed: porosity 31.8 → 25.1 → 16.7 → 16.5 % (final state relaxed at 
fixed platen); 7:3 (large : small NCM) is the lowest of the five beds.

4Battery Materials Lab.
 From the contact network to Li⁺ transport
• Kirchhoff network: each SE–SE contact = bulk resistance + Holm/Maxwell 
constriction using Hertz contact radii; σ₀ = 1.5 mS cm⁻¹ [8].
• T ransport tortuosity T = φ_SE σ₀ / σ_eff: 7.2 → 5.0 (0:10 → 7:3). Contact 
constriction accounts for 73–75 % of Joule dissipation in this network model.

5Battery Materials Lab.
 What a fixed-shape soft-sphere DEM cannot do
• No shape change and no yield cap: overlap is the only plasticity proxy; the 
softened SE modulus (1.35 vs ≈ 22 GPa) is an effective parameter, not a 
property [1, 7].
• In one 7:3 bed, global viscous damping carries 58 % of the plate reaction 
during compression — an open issue.
DEM

(22 studies; author classification)
· softened SE modulus: 0/22
· yield or hardness cap: 7/22

none

6Battery Materials Lab.
 The material point method supplies the plastic half
• J2 plasticity on a background grid: shape change and void filling that a 
fixed-shape sphere cannot represent.
• Active material is kept rigid (DEM skeleton); only the electrolyte flows. 2D: E 
= 1.53 GPa, σy = 0.15 GPa; 3D: E = 1.53 GPa, ν = 0.49, σy = 0.30 GPa.

7Battery Materials Lab.
MPM
 Effective material inputs and their status
• Bulk modulus from DFT; shear softening and yield stress from a pure-
electrolyte calibration sweep.
Effective material inputs
• Bulk LPSCl: E ≈ 22 GPa (DFT; DEM 
input 22.1 GPa [8]); σy 0.05–0.30 GPa
• DEM effective: E = 1.35 GPa — 
reproduces compaction, not a 
property
• MPM: E = 1.53 GPa, ν = 0.49, σy = 
0.30 GPa; K = 25.5 ≈ DFT 26.2 GPa
Calibration target and limits
• Calibration target: pure-SE porosity 10 
% at 300 MPa (lab reference sample, 
unpublished)
• Not a literature anchor; the earlier 
attribution was withdrawn
• Shear-only softening keeps the real 
bulk modulus (ν = 0.49)
T ested alternatives (volumetric cap, real E) did not remove the need for effective 
parameters.

8Battery Materials Lab.
 Compaction agreement depends on initialization and loading 
protocol
• Historical and current scaffold calculations differ in electrolyte initialization 
and loading protocol; they are not one validation series.
• AM load sharing remains a candidate explanation for over-compaction; the 
final hypothesis verdict is pending.
MPM
Scaffold calculations (AM skeleton from the DEM bed)
· Earlier: cell-filled SE, bidirectional servo — historical, not a DEM-seeded validation
· Current registered runs: DEM-seeded SE, fixed-platen hold — f = 0 completed; f(a) 
execution failed
· AM-load-sharing hypothesis: verdict pending

9Battery Materials Lab.
 Voxelizing the compacted microstructure into a transport mesh
• Finite-volume conservation on the phase grid gives electrical (σ, φ) and 
thermal (κ, T) transport on the same structure.
• Faces are joined by a harmonic mean with no interface-resistance term: an 
ideal-interface voxel model — an upper bound only within the same 
geometry, properties and boundaries.

10Battery Materials Lab.
 Additive geometry used in transport rasterization
• Carbon fibres (VGCF) as diameter-preserving segments, PTFE as a centre-
line insulator, a conductive polymer as true-diameter spheres.
• Pre-registered 104-arm study: the electronic-conductivity order across 1–4 
wt% VGCF holds across the tested voxel sizes and grid-origin offsets 
(72/72).

 Problem 1: Grid dependence
• The electronic ratio decreases across the three tested voxel spacings (0.4, 
0.3, 0.25 µm); the ionic ratio crosses 1.
• Grid convergence has not been established.

13Battery Materials Lab.
 Problem 3: Load sharing during compaction
• NCM–NCM contacts contribute 48–60 % of vertical stress after relaxation at 
fixed platen position; 7:3 is the minimum.
• The porosity ranking agrees for the selected five compositions (exploratory 
comparison, n = 5).

14Battery Materials Lab.
Progress
 Registered studies and current status
• Registered before launch, reviewed externally; the table shows the ledger 
state, not result claims.
Study status
1. Historical eight-origin study Conductivity estimates and inference remain

2. VGCF ordering study (104 arms) Ordering holds across tested grids and

5. Updated transport software Seven reviews completed; production 
remains pending

15Battery Materials Lab.
 A 194-bed design-of-experiments dataset for machine learning
• 130 + 64 Latin-hypercube beds (composition, particle sizes) → structure and 
transport descriptors, released as v1.2 (conditional use as model 
descriptors).
• SE percolation 106/130; geometric shortest-path tortuosity 1.3–4.2 
(percolating beds; not transport tortuosity).

17Battery Materials Lab.
Summary
 Current findings and limitations
• DEM and contact networks: composition trends from one bed per 
composition
• MPM: plastic deformation, with compaction agreement dependent on 
initialization and loading protocol
• Voxel transport: ideal-interface calculations with grid dependence and 
unresolved absolute conductivity
• Final model-validation verdicts remain pending
